Builds test arguments for {@code hasOption} parameterized tests.

Each row contains: (args, opt, optionGroup, optDep, has, grpDep, hasGrp, grpOpt) where {@code optDep}/{@code grpDep} indicate whether the deprecation handler should fire when querying via {@code opt}/{@code optionGroup} respectively.
Querying optT (the deprecated option): opt parameter = optT -T/--tee in args: T is present — has=true, deprecation fires for both opt and group
-U/--you in args: T is absent — has=false, no deprecation for optT; group selected U (non-deprecated)
Querying optU (the non-deprecated option): opt parameter = optU -T/--tee in args: U is absent — has=false, no deprecation for optU; group selected T (deprecated)
-U/--you in args: U is present — has=true, no deprecation (U is not deprecated); group selected U

Builds test arguments for {@code getOptionValue} parameterized tests.

Each row contains: (args, opt, optionGroup, optDep, optValue, grpDep, grpValue, grpOpt) where {@code optDep}/{@code grpDep} indicate whether the deprecation handler should fire and {@code optValue}/{@code grpValue} are the expected string values.
Querying optT (the deprecated option): opt parameter = optT -T/--tee in args: T is present — deprecation fires, value comes from T
-U/--you in args: T is absent — no deprecation for optT, value from U belongs to group only
Querying optU (the non-deprecated option): opt parameter = optU -T/--tee in args: U is absent — no deprecation for optU; group selected T (deprecated)
-U/--you in args: U is present — value comes from U, no deprecation (U is not deprecated)

Builds test arguments for {@code getOptionValues} parameterized tests.

Each row contains: (args, opt, optionGroup, optDep, optValue, grpDep, grpValue, grpOpt) where values are String arrays (options accept two arguments each).
Querying optT (the deprecated option): opt parameter = optT -T/--tee in args: T is present — deprecation fires, values come from T
-U/--you in args: T is absent — no deprecation for optT, values from U belong to group only
Querying optU (the non-deprecated option): opt parameter = optU -T/--tee in args: U is absent — no deprecation for optU; group selected T (deprecated)
-U/--you in args: U is present — values come from U, no deprecation (U is not deprecated)

Builds test arguments for {@code getParsedOptionValue} parameterized tests.

Each row contains: (args, opt, optionGroup, optDep, optValue, grpDep, grpValue, grpOpt) where values are parsed {@code Integer} objects (options have type {@code Integer.class}).
Querying optT (the deprecated option): opt parameter = optT -T/--tee in args: T is present — deprecation fires, parsed value comes from T
-U/--you in args: T is absent — no deprecation for optT, parsed value from U belongs to group only
Querying optU (the non-deprecated option): opt parameter = optU -T/--tee in args: U is absent — no deprecation for optU; group selected T (deprecated)
-U/--you in args: U is present — parsed value comes from U, no deprecation (U is not deprecated)

Builds test arguments for {@code getParsedOptionValues} parameterized tests.

Each row contains: (args, opt, optionGroup, optDep, optValue, grpDep, grpValue, grpOpt) where values are parsed {@code Integer} arrays (options accept multiple args with type {@code Integer.class}).
Querying optT (the deprecated option): opt parameter = optT -T/--tee in args: T is present — deprecation fires, parsed values come from T
-U/--you in args: T is absent — no deprecation for optT, parsed values from U belong to group only
Querying optU (the non-deprecated option): opt parameter = optU -T/--tee in args: U is absent — no deprecation for optU; group selected T (deprecated)
-U/--you in args: U is present — parsed values come from U, no deprecation (U is not deprecated)
Returns the first character of the option's short name, for use with char-based API overloads.

Asserts that the deprecation notice for option T was printed to stdout exactly once (or not at all), then clears the captured output so the next assertion starts from a clean state. @param shouldHavePrinted {@code true} if the deprecation message is expected in the output. @param capturedOutput the byte stream capturing stdout.

Asserts that the deprecation handler was triggered exactly once with the expected option (or not at all), then clears the log so the next assertion starts from a clean state. @param shouldHaveFired {@code true} if the handler should have been called once. @param deprecationLog the list that collects options passed to the deprecation handler. @param expectedOption the option expected to have triggered the handler; ignored when {@code shouldHaveFired} is {@code false}.
